title: Making a red
subtitle: Colour, tannin and pressing
objectives: Describe the steps of red winemaking
Explain the ways to extract colour and tannin

steps.title: The steps
steps.body: Black grapes are destemmed and crushed. Juice, skins and seeds ferment together, often at 25 to 30 degrees. The skins float to the top and form a cap. After fermentation the wine may stay on the skins to extract more, then is pressed. The free-run wine and the press wine are kept separate.

steps.title: Managing the cap
steps.body: The cap of skins must be kept in contact with the juice to extract colour and tannin and to stop it drying out and spoiling. Punching down pushes the cap under. Pumping over sprays juice from the bottom over the top. Rack and return drains the tank and pours the juice back. Each gives a different intensity of extraction.
steps.highlight: Punch down, pump over, rack and return

steps.prompt: Why must the cap of skins be managed during red fermentation?
options: To extract colour and tannin and avoid spoilage
steps.explanation: A floating cap dries out and can spoil. Keeping it wet extracts colour, tannin and flavour.

steps.title: Carbonic maceration
steps.body: In carbonic maceration, whole bunches go into a tank filled with carbon dioxide. Fermentation starts inside each berry, without yeast at first. This gives soft, low-tannin reds with bright aromas of banana, bubblegum and cherry. It is the classic method of Beaujolais, where many wines use a partial version.
steps.highlight: Whole berries, CO2, fruity soft reds

steps.prompt: Which are ways to extract colour and tannin from the cap?
steps.explanation: Cold settling is used to clear white juice, not to manage a red cap.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Reds ferment with their skins, then are pressed
Punching down, pumping over and rack and return manage extraction
Carbonic maceration gives soft, fruity reds like Beaujolais
